body.en:
Question B-001-007-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Turning down background audio helps prevent retransmitting music or other non-amateur signals through the microphone.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Turn up the volume of your transmitter": More transmitter audio or power would make pickup more likely to be transmitted, not less.
- sourceIndex 2: "Speak closer to the microphone to increase your signal strength": Speaking closer does not remove the non-amateur audio source in the room.
- sourceIndex 3: "Adjust your transceiver noise blanker": A receiver noise blanker does not stop the microphone from picking up background audio.
